facts.statement: Elbretornis was an extinct genus of enantiornithine birds that lived in what is now Salta Province, Argentina, during the late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Elbretornis is an extinct genus of enantiornithine which existed in what is now Salta Province, Argentina during the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The genus Elbretornis and its only known species, Elbretornis bonapartei, were named by Cyril A. Walker and Gareth J. Dyke in 2009.
facts.quote: It was named by Cyril A. Walker and Gareth J. Dyke in 2009, and the type and so far only species is Elbretornis bonapartei.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Elbretornis indicates the animal was 33 cm long, had a hip height of 24 cm, and weighed 570 g.
facts.quote: The holotype indicates an animal with a length of 33 cm, hip height of 24 cm, and weight of 570 g.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Elbretornis is a distinct genus or if it actually belongs to previously described genera like Lectavis, Soroavisaurus, or Yungavolucris due to the scarcity of known fossil elements.
facts.quote: As few elements are known from Elbretornis, it might actually belong to one of the El Brete enantiornithines known only from leg bones and described earlier, namely Lectavis, Soroavisaurus or Yungavolucris.

facts.statement: Elbretornis bonapartei lived approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vivió hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años.

facts.statement: Like other enantiornithines, Elbretornis bones were highly pneumatized, implying an adaptation for flight.
facts.quote: Al igual que otras Enantiornithes, una de las características más notables es que sus huesos están altamente neumatizados, implicando una adaptación al vuelo.

facts.statement: Besides the holotype, fossils of other specimens include dorsal vertebrae, a sacrum, a femur, a rib, and a tibiotarsus.
facts.quote: Además del holotipo, también se han descubierto algunos elementos de otros especímenes. Estos corresponden a vértebras dorsales, un sinsacro, un fémur, una costilla y un tibiotarso.

facts.statement: Elbretornis lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Elbretornis is known from the holotype PVL 4022, which includes a left humerus and associated right radius, ulna, scapula, coracoid, and tibiotarsus found in the Maastrichtian-age Lecho Formation of Argentina.
rejected.quote: It is known from the holotype PVL 4022, left humerus and associated right radius, ulna, scapula, coracoid, and tibiotarsus, recovered from the El Brete locality (Maastrichtian age), Lecho Formation of Argentina.
